root.name: Grünfeld Defense: Opocensky Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. e3 O-O 6. Bd2

overview: White builds a quiet Three Knights centre with e3 and Bd2, aiming for Be2 and castling rather than a big pawn centre. Black strikes at d4 with ...c5 or ...Bg4 and ...Nc6, keeping the g7 bishop on the long diagonal. The game is a positional fight over the d4/d5 pawns, with little early forcing play.

white_ideas.idea: Complete development with Bd2, Be2 and O-O
Keep d4 supported with the solid e3-d4 centre

black_ideas.idea: Pressure d4 along the long diagonal with ...Bg7 and ...Nc6

typical_structures.structure: Grünfeld with White pawns on c4, d4, e3 and Black pressure on d4

character.notes: Quiet for both: White avoids the Exchange centre and Black has easy counterplay.

structure.notes: The d5/c4/d4 tension is unresolved and the centre stays fluid.

approach.notes: A named Grünfeld line used at club and master level.

level.notes: Black needs to understand the ...c5 break rather than memorise long lines.
